sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、扎伊尔兰·蒙达尼等许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日要闻。

sentences.en: More than 26,000 fires have been recorded inside the Amazon rainforest in August alone, triggering global calls for action.
sentences.zh: 仅在8月，亚马逊雨林内就记录了超过26,000起火灾，引发了全球采取行动的呼声。

sentences.en: So why is Brazil's government telling the rest of the world to mind its own business?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么巴西政府告诉世界其他国家不要多管闲事呢？

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月28日，星期三。

sentences.en: Through the prism of Twitter or Facebook, I think a lot of people last week understandably engaged in this, like, communal panic about the fate of the world's largest rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 通过Twitter或Facebook的视角，我认为上周很多人都在情理之中地陷入了一种集体恐慌，担心这片世界上最大的雨林的命运。

sentences.en: Ernesto Londano covers Brazil for The Times.
sentences.zh: 埃内斯托·隆达诺为《纽约时报》报道巴西新闻。

sentences.en: Urgent pleas to save the rainforest as the Amazon burns.
sentences.zh: 随着亚马逊燃烧，拯救雨林的呼声日益紧迫。

sentences.en: Forest fires are raging in the rainforeSt. There have been nearly 73,000 fires this year already, a more than 80% increase compared to last year.
sentences.zh: 雨林中森林大火肆虐。今年已经发生了近73,000起火灾，与去年相比增加了80%以上。

sentences.en: With international protests, the world is demanding action.
sentences.zh: 随着国际抗议活动的开展，全世界都在要求采取行动。

sentences.en: The French president, Emmanuel Macron, has described the fires as an international emergency.
sentences.zh: 法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙将这些火灾描述为国际紧急事件。

sentences.en: You were seeing presidents, you were seeing celebrities.
sentences.zh: 你看到了总统们，也看到了名人们。

sentences.en: And actor Leonardo DiCaprio working to help combat the wildfires in the Amazon rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 还有演员莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥致力于帮助扑灭亚马逊雨林的野火。

sentences.en: The climate change...
sentences.zh: 气候变化……

sentences.en: You were seeing these really alarming posts and these photographs of patches of the rainforest on fire.
sentences.zh: 你看到了那些非常令人震惊的帖子，以及雨林部分地区着火的照片。

sentences.en: The smoke is traveling far and wide.
sentences.zh: 烟雾正在四处蔓延。

sentences.en: I think many people, understandably, were left with the impression that, you know, within a few days, the Amazon was going to be reduced to a pile of ashes.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多人理所当然地留下了这样一种印象：亚马逊可能在几天之内就会化为灰烬。

sentences.en: The Amazon rainforest, the so-called lungs of the world, are now filling with smoke.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊雨林，这个所谓的“地球之肺”，现在正被烟雾填满。

sentences.en: I think, in many people's minds, there was a clear villain in all of this.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在许多人的心目中，这一切都有一个明确的恶棍。

sentences.en: Directly blaming the record fires in the Amazon on Brazilian president...
sentences.zh: 直接将亚马逊创纪录的火灾归咎于巴西总统……

sentences.en: The president of Brazil, Jair Bolsonaro, who has shifted his government's approach on the environment in a really traumatic way.
sentences.zh: 巴西总统雅伊尔·博索纳罗，他以一种非常激进的方式改变了政府的环境方针。

sentences.en: ...scientists warn this could be a devastating blow to the fight against climate change.
sentences.zh: ……科学家警告称，这可能对气候变化斗争造成毁灭性打击。

sentences.en: And this is certainly a story about climate change.
sentences.zh: 这当然是一个关于气候变化的故事。

sentences.en: And it's a story about President Bolsonaro.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个关于博索纳罗总统的故事。

sentences.en: But it's a far more complicated story than we've been hearing.
sentences.zh: 但它比我们所听到的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: So where should we start this story?
sentences.zh: 那么我们应该从哪里开始讲这个故事呢？

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's important to think about the history of the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为思考亚马逊的历史很重要。

sentences.en: The great Amazon River of South America is so deep and so wide that the people of Brazil call it the River Sea.
sentences.zh: 南美洲伟大的亚马逊河深而宽，以至于巴西人称其为“河海”。

sentences.en: I think for decades, the Amazon captured people's imagination in a way that few places on Earth did.
sentences.zh: 我认为几十年来，亚马逊以地球上极少数地方所能及的方式激发了人们的想象力。

sentences.en: The tropical rainforest biome is a complex community exceedingly rich in many forms of plant and animal life, a showplace of natural history.
sentences.zh: 热带雨林生物群落是一个复杂的群落，拥有极其丰富的动植物生命形式，是自然历史的展示场。

sentences.en: It was, you know, this mysterious and dangerous place that drew adventurers and scientists and botanists.
sentences.zh: 它曾经是一个神秘而危险的地方，吸引着探险家、科学家和植物学家。

sentences.en: Through ceaseless evolution, a display of flora and fauna has developed here, unequaled anywhere else on land.
sentences.zh: 通过不断的进化，这里发展出了一套陆地上其他任何地方都无法比拟的动植物群。

sentences.en: And, you know, for many, many years, it was kind of these images of this raw wildlife and kind of the mystique that laid under the canopy that people were fascinated by.
sentences.zh: 多年来，人们一直对这些原始野生动物的影像以及树冠下隐藏的神秘感着迷。

sentences.en: Moist, always green forests still cover one-tenth of the Earth's land surface and comprise a large part of the total forest area of the world.
sentences.zh: 潮湿、常绿的森林覆盖了地球陆地表面的十分之一，占世界森林总面积的很大一部分。

sentences.en: It contains the largest supply of fresh water in the world, and it's just teeming with biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 它拥有世界上最大的淡水供应，并且充满了生物多样性。

sentences.en: But in the 1970s, the Brazilian government, which was then led by military rulers, decided it was time to settle this vast rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 但在20世纪70年代，当时由军政府领导的巴西政府决定是时候开发这片广阔的雨林了。

sentences.en: The conquest of Western Brazil began in 1970 with the construction of the Trans-Amazonian Highway.
sentences.zh: 对巴西西部的征服始于1970年，当时修建了跨亚马逊公路。

sentences.en: And it created a road that cut through the Amazon and started encouraging people to move there and to start making a living there.
sentences.zh: 这条公路穿过了亚马逊，并开始鼓励人们搬到那里，开始在那里谋生。

sentences.en: The dense bush gave way to large buildings where mining equipment is kept and to silos, which today hold a harvest of mineral plenty.
sentences.zh: 茂密的灌木丛让位于存放采矿设备的大型建筑和筒仓，如今这些筒仓里装满了矿产资源。

sentences.en: Their view was that the Amazon contained tons of resources, minerals, land that could be converted into farmland,
sentences.zh: 他们的观点是，亚马逊蕴藏着大量的资源、矿产和土地，可以转化为农田，

sentences.en: and that it was time to turn it into an economic engine for Brazil.
sentences.zh: 是时候把它变成巴西的经济引擎了。

sentences.en: The dream of gold, a heady prospect which has set men's hearts on fire since ancient times.
sentences.zh: 黄金梦，这个自古以来就让男人心潮澎湃的诱人前景。

sentences.en: In modern-day Brazil, they've torn the Earth asunder for it.
sentences.zh: 在现代巴西，他们为了黄金将大地撕裂。

sentences.en: When it starts happening initially, you know, people realise that things are changing, but there's no real alarm until a few years later when things get really out of control.
sentences.zh: 当它最初开始发生时，人们意识到事情正在发生变化，但在几年后事情真正失控之前，并没有真正的警觉。

sentences.en: All that glitters may indeed be gold and beautiful once it's cleaned.
sentences.zh: 所有闪光的东西一旦清洗干净，确实可能是金子，非常美丽。

sentences.en: But any short-term profits come not without a price to be paid.
sentences.zh: 但任何短期利润都必须付出代价。

sentences.en: Where trees start getting chopped down at a really staggering rate.
sentences.zh: 树木开始以惊人的速度被砍伐。

sentences.en: And that price is turning out to be high for humans and animals alike.
sentences.zh: 而这个代价对人类和动物来说都变得非常高昂。

sentences.en: And people start realising that the world's largest rainforest is being destroyed, is atrophying at an astonishing speed.
sentences.zh: 人们开始意识到，世界上最大的雨林正在被摧毁，正以惊人的速度萎缩。

sentences.en: These are some Indian friends of mine in the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 这些是我在亚马逊的一些印第安朋友。

sentences.en: Their lives today are in great danger.
sentences.zh: 他们今天的生活处于极大的危险之中。

sentences.en: Their beautiful home in the rainforest is being destroyed by logging, mining and ranching.
sentences.zh: 他们在雨林中美丽的家园正被伐木、采矿和畜牧业摧毁。

sentences.en: This sparks worldwide consternation, and people start asking whether the Amazon might cease to exist one day if it continues to be destroyed at this rate.
sentences.zh: 这引发了全世界的震惊，人们开始质疑，如果继续以这种速度被破坏，亚马逊有一天是否会不复存在。

sentences.en: This is the rainforest in 30 years if present trends continue.
sentences.zh: 如果目前的趋势持续下去，这就是30年后的雨林。

sentences.en: It's all gone.
sentences.zh: 一切都消失了。

sentences.en: The lungs of the Earth destroyed.
sentences.zh: 地球之肺被摧毁了。

sentences.en: You know, you had politicians, you had artists, you had songs about this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时有政客、艺术家，还有关于此的歌曲。

sentences.en: It really became a cultural moment.
sentences.zh: 这确实成为了一个文化时刻。

sentences.en: People became very invested in this idea that everybody had a role to play in saving the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 人们非常投入于这样一个理念：每个人在拯救亚马逊的过程中都扮演着一个角色。

sentences.en: Right, this is the Save the Rainforest campaign.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是“拯救雨林”运动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And does this movement have an effect in Brazil?
sentences.zh: 那么这场运动在巴西有影响吗？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: But I think it's important to note that it is greeted with very deep skepticism and, to an extent, paranoia in some circles.
sentences.zh: 但我认为值得注意的是，它在某些圈子里受到了非常深刻的怀疑，甚至在某种程度上是偏执。

sentences.en: I think there's long been a view among conservative nationalist Brazilians
sentences.zh: 我认为保守的民族主义巴西人长期以来一直有一种观点，

sentences.en: that all this outcry about the fate of the rainforest was really a veiled attempt to keep Brazil from developing its God-given potential.
sentences.zh: 即所有关于雨林命运的呼声，实际上都是为了阻止巴西发挥其天赋潜力的隐蔽企图。

sentences.en: I think many Brazilians saw these calls to preserve the Amazon as infringing its sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多巴西人认为这些保护亚马逊的呼吁是在侵犯其主权。

sentences.en: And for many years, they were pretty dismissive about this, and they said that the fate of the Amazon was only for Brazil
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们对此相当不屑一顾，并表示亚马逊的命运只能由巴西

sentences.en: and its neighbors to think about, debate about, and decide on.
sentences.zh: 及其邻国来思考、辩论和决定。

sentences.en: So what happens to this development of the Amazon?
sentences.zh: 那么亚马逊的这种开发发生了什么？

sentences.en: During the 1990s and the early 2000s, we see deforestation reaching really staggering levels.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代和21世纪初，我们看到森林砍伐达到了惊人的程度。

sentences.en: Concern around the world, I think, reaches a point where the Brazilians can no longer ignore what people outside of the country were saying about this.
sentences.zh: 我认为世界各地的担忧达到了一个临界点，巴西人再也无法忽视国外对这件事的议论了。

sentences.en: So when President Lula, a leftist, is in office in the early 2000s, he appoints a woman who was from the rainforest to serve as his minister of the environment.
sentences.zh: 因此，当左翼人士卢拉总统在21世纪初上任时，他任命了一位来自雨林的女性担任环境部长。

sentences.en: Her name is Marina Silva.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫玛丽娜·席尔瓦。

sentences.en: And she came up with a really bold and ambitious plan to rein in deforestation and create more conservation areas.
sentences.zh: 她提出了一个非常大胆和雄心勃勃的计划，旨在遏制森林砍伐并建立更多的保护区。

sentences.en: You know, she was somebody who was lauded across the world for doing something that people thought was almost impossible,
sentences.zh: 她因做到了人们认为几乎不可能的事情而受到全世界的赞誉，

sentences.en: to sort of stop these loggers and these miners and these farmers from reaching deeper and deeper into the Amazon year after year after year.
sentences.zh: 即阻止这些伐木工、矿工和农民年复一年地深入亚马逊腹地。

sentences.en: And for a while, Brazil was pretty successful.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，巴西相当成功。

sentences.en: So all of this outcry leads Brazil to begin regulating and slowing this development.
sentences.zh: 所以所有的这些呼声促使巴西开始监管并减缓这种开发。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Another thing the government did was it started issuing some pretty stiff fines for deforestation and other environmental crimes.
sentences.zh: 政府做的另一件事是开始对森林砍伐和其他环境犯罪处以相当严厉的罚款。

sentences.en: And, you know, for a while, this had the intended effect.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，这确实达到了预期的效果。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons Brazil was successful in reigning in deforestation during this era is the economy was doing pretty well.
sentences.zh: 巴西在这个时期成功遏制森林砍伐的原因之一是经济状况相当不错。

sentences.en: So there were plenty of jobs in the city and people were less tempted to venture deep into the jungle where they faced the risk of fines.
sentences.zh: 所以城市里有很多工作机会，人们不太愿意冒险深入丛林，因为那里面临着罚款的风险。

sentences.en: However, you know, the good days came to an end.
sentences.zh: 然而，好日子到头了。

sentences.en: And in 2014, the country plunged into a brutal recession.
sentences.zh: 2014年，该国陷入了残酷的经济衰退。

sentences.en: And what this meant was tens of thousands of men were suddenly unemployed and many of them were lured back into the jungle.
sentences.zh: 这意味着成千上万的男人突然失业，许多人被引诱回丛林。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because there was money to be made.
sentences.zh: 因为那里有钱可赚。

sentences.en: These were dangerous jobs.
sentences.zh: 这些都是危险的工作。

sentences.en: These were risky ventures.
sentences.zh: 这些都是冒险的勾当。

sentences.en: But for many people, it was the only way to put food on the table.
sentences.zh: 但对许多人来说，这是维持生计的唯一途径。

sentences.en: And so the deforestation started all over again.
sentences.zh: 于是森林砍伐又开始了。

sentences.en: Deforestation starts climbing again.
sentences.zh: 森林砍伐再次攀升。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能获取所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当您第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，您在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间跨越付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Ernesto, so a recession hits and deforestation is back on the rise.
sentences.zh: 埃内斯托，经济衰退来袭，森林砍伐又呈上升趋势。

sentences.en: What does this mean for resilience?
sentences.zh: 这对恢复力意味着什么？

sentences.en: So around this time, many people who were being fined for violating environmental laws were refusing to pay.
sentences.zh: 大约在这个时候，许多因违反环境法而被罚款的人拒绝支付。

sentences.en: And, you know, sense that they could get away with it.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得可以逃脱惩罚。

sentences.en: And among them was a then-congressman, Jair Bolsonaro, who was allegedly busted fishing in a wildlife reserve.
sentences.zh: 其中就包括时任国会议员的雅伊尔·博索纳罗，他据称在野生动物保护区非法捕鱼时被抓。

sentences.en: He refused to identify himself when the agent saw him.
sentences.zh: 当特工发现他时，他拒绝表明身份。

sentences.en: But the agent recognized him, took his picture, documented that he was in a wildlife reserve, and issued him a citation.
sentences.zh: 但特工认出了他，拍下了他的照片，记录下他在野生动物保护区的事实，并向他开出了传票。

sentences.en: Bolsonaro never bothered to pay his fine.
sentences.zh: 博索纳罗从没打算支付罚款。

sentences.en: And then last year, when he's running for president and when he becomes a frontrunner,
sentences.zh: 去年，当他竞选总统并成为领跑者时，

sentences.en: Mr. Bolsonaro said that the fines that were issued by this agency amounted to a racket.
sentences.zh: 博索纳罗先生称该机构开出的罚款简直是敲诈。

sentences.en: He called it an industry that needed to be shut down.
sentences.zh: 他称这是一个需要被取缔的行业。

sentences.en: So Bolsonaro, when he campaigns for president, does so by kind of flagrantly disregarding the environmental protections of the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 所以博索纳罗在竞选总统时，公然无视亚马逊的环境保护措施。

sentences.en: And it seems like by tapping into this long-standing nationalist view that the Amazon is a Brazilian resource that Brazilians should be tapping into.
sentences.zh: 他似乎利用了这种长期存在的民族主义观点，即亚马逊是巴西的资源，巴西人应该对其进行开发。

sentences.en: And any effort to stop that is kind of a globalist intervention, and it will hurt Brazil.
sentences.zh: 任何阻止这种开发的努力都是一种全球主义干预，会伤害巴西。

sentences.en: That's right, Michael.
sentences.zh: 没错，迈克尔。

sentences.en: But he wasn't only angry about environmental fines.
sentences.zh: 但他不仅对环境罚款感到愤怒。

sentences.en: He was also very frustrated with indigenous territories.
sentences.zh: 他对原住民领地也非常不满。

sentences.en: These are territories that now cover about 13% of Brazil's landmass.
sentences.zh: 这些领地目前覆盖了巴西约13%的土地面积。

sentences.en: And Mr. Bolsonaro spoke in unusually hostile terms about indigenous people.
sentences.zh: 博索纳罗先生以异常敌对的言辞谈论原住民。

sentences.en: He essentially said you have these small indigenous communities sitting on land that could be extremely profitable.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，这些小规模的原住民社区坐拥着可能带来巨额利润的土地。

sentences.en: And they should be allowed to bring in outsiders to set up mining camps, to develop farmland, to start producing wealth.
sentences.zh: 应该允许他们引入外来者建立采矿营地、开发农田、开始创造财富。

sentences.en: And so his solution, it sounds like, is to develop more and more of the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 所以他的解决方案听起来就是开发越来越多的亚马逊。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And when he wins, he wastes no time on delivering on his campaign promises on this front.
sentences.zh: 当他获胜后，他毫不拖延地兑现了他在这一方面的竞选承诺。

sentences.en: One of his first steps in office was to give the Ministry of Agriculture control over the process of adjudicating any new indigenous territories.
sentences.zh: 他上任后的第一步措施之一，就是将任何新原住民领地的裁决权交给农业部。

sentences.en: It was essentially kind of giving the people who had an interest in developing these territories and in changing their nature entirely the keys to the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 这本质上是把钥匙交给了那些有兴趣开发这些领地并彻底改变其性质的人。

sentences.en: You know, environmentalists and indigenous activists were appalled, and they braced for a bruising fight.
sentences.zh: 环保人士和原住民活动家感到震惊，他们准备迎接一场激烈的斗争。

sentences.en: So what happens when Bolsonaro starts making these changes across the government and allowing for more development of the Amazon?
sentences.zh: 那么，当博索纳罗开始在政府内部进行这些改革并允许更多地开发亚马逊时，发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, even before any new laws or regulations came to fruition, I think people out in the countryside felt emboldened.
sentences.zh: 嗯，甚至在任何新法律或法规出台之前，我认为农村地区的人们就感到胆子更大了。

sentences.en: And we started hearing anecdotes of miners and of loggers striding into indigenous territories and other protected areas in a way that was more visible and bolder than they had before.
sentences.zh: 我们开始听到矿工和伐木工大摇大摆地进入原住民领地和其他保护区的轶事，其方式比以前更显眼、更大胆。

sentences.en: What we also see is a sharp rise in deforestation.
sentences.zh: 我们还看到森林砍伐急剧上升。

sentences.en: During the first six months of the Bolsonaro era, deforestation increased by roughly 40 percent.
sentences.zh: 在博索纳罗执政的前六个月里，森林砍伐增加了约40%。

sentences.en: And historically, the rate of deforestation has been closely linked to the prevalence of forest fires.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，森林砍伐率与森林火灾的发生率密切相关。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this is what we're seeing in all these photos online.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们在网上所有这些照片中看到的情况。

sentences.en: The Amazon is on fire and it's rampant deforestation under Bolsonaro that has caused it.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊雨林正在燃烧，而博索纳罗治下猖獗的森林砍伐正是罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there were literally thousands of fires burning across the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊雨林中确实有数以千计的火点在燃烧。

sentences.en: But I think what many people didn't quite understand was that this happens every year.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很多人没完全搞明白的是，这种情况每年都会发生。

sentences.en: Around this time when it tends to be cooler and drier across the Amazon,
sentences.zh: 在亚马逊地区气候趋于凉爽干燥的这段时间里，

sentences.en: there's sort of a slash and burn cycle that happens where farmers and people who have logged patches of the Amazon clear the bush and set it on fire.
sentences.zh: 通常会有一种“刀耕火种”的循环，农民和砍伐过雨林地块的人会清理灌木丛并放火焚烧。

sentences.en: And most of these fires tend to be relatively small and relatively contained.
sentences.zh: 大多数火灾规模相对较小，也相对可控。

sentences.en: But something was different this year.
sentences.zh: 但今年情况有些不同。

sentences.en: The number was unusually high.
sentences.zh: 火灾数量异常之高。

sentences.en: You know, so far this month, there's been more than 26,000 fires detected through satellite imagery.
sentences.zh: 你知道，本月到目前为止，卫星图像已经探测到超过26000处火点。

sentences.en: That's more than twice the number of fires registered last year.
sentences.zh: 这比去年登记的火灾数量多出了一倍多。

sentences.en: But this was by no means an all time high.
sentences.zh: 但这绝非历史最高水平。

sentences.en: You know, we've seen other periods in years past when there were far more fires burning across the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 你知道，过去我们也见过火灾规模远超今年的时期。

sentences.en: I think what was different this year is you had all these alarming and widely shared posts on social media, some of which were using pictures that were many, many years old,
sentences.zh: 我认为今年不同之处在于，社交媒体上出现了大量令人震惊且被广泛转发的帖子，其中一些甚至使用了多年前的照片，

sentences.en: that weren't really an accurate reflection of what was happening on the ground this year.
sentences.zh: 这些照片并不能准确反映今年当地的真实情况。

sentences.en: So what do you make of that, this response, which has been so enormous, and the history and reality of this situation in Brazil?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何看待这种反响——如此巨大的舆论浪潮，以及巴西这一问题的历史与现实？

sentences.en: Clearly, it has put a spotlight on a problem that is very real and very serious.
sentences.zh: 显然，它让一个非常真实且严重的问题受到了关注。

sentences.en: The Amazon is shrinking at a rate that many scientists call unsustainable.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊雨林正以许多科学家所称的“不可持续”的速度萎缩。

sentences.en: They fear that it's approaching a so-called tipping point where large sections turn into savannah and where it might be impossible to turn it back into, you know, lush,
sentences.zh: 他们担心雨林正接近所谓的“临界点”，大片区域可能退化为稀树草原，届时可能再也无法恢复成那种郁郁葱葱、

sentences.en: thick rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 茂密的热带雨林了。

sentences.en: However,
sentences.zh: 然而，

sentences.en: I think the way this story got off the ground may have been counterproductive for the international community to engage the Brazilian government and its very impulsive leader in a constructive debate.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个故事的传播方式，可能反而不利于国际社会与巴西政府及其行事冲动的领导人进行建设性的辩论。

sentences.en: The European leaders threatened to scrap a major trade deal.
sentences.zh: 欧洲领导人威胁要废除一项重大贸易协定。

sentences.en: Brazil last week faced the prospect that a trade deal that Brazil and a few neighboring countries reached with the European Union could be nixed.
sentences.zh: 上周，巴西面临着一项巴西及几个邻国与欧盟达成的贸易协定可能被取消的风险。

sentences.en: I think there's going to be an international reaction to boycott Brazilian food just to proteSt.
sentences.zh: 我想国际社会可能会通过抵制巴西食品来表达抗议。

sentences.en: There were calls to boycott Brazilian products.
sentences.zh: 当时确实出现了抵制巴西产品的呼声。

sentences.en: French President Emmanuel Macron is now calling the fires an international crisis that should be on the agenda at the G7 summit this weekend in France.
sentences.zh: 法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙现在将这些火灾称为一场国际危机，并认为这应该列入本周末在法国举行的七国集团（G7）峰会议程。

sentences.en: And the G7 leaders who were about to have their conference in France said that this was going to be a last minute high profile item added to the agenda.
sentences.zh: 而即将举行会议的七国集团领导人表示，这将作为最后一刻加入议程的高规格议题。

sentences.en: Brazil, I think, understandably said, wait a minute, how are you going to discuss the fate of the Amazon when we're not at the table?
sentences.zh: 我认为巴西的反应是可以理解的，他们说：等等，当我们不在谈判桌上时，你们怎么能讨论亚马逊的命运呢？

sentences.en: This makes no sense.
sentences.zh: 这毫无道理。

sentences.en: G7 leaders agreeing to a $20 million financial aid package to help Brazil fight the fires in the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 七国集团领导人同意提供2000万美元的经济援助，以帮助巴西扑灭亚马逊雨林的火灾。

sentences.en: And even as pledges of emergency aid started being dangled by European leaders and by organizations that, you know, wanted to take some immediate and urgent action on these fires,
sentences.zh: 即便欧洲领导人和一些想要对这些火灾采取紧急行动的组织开始抛出紧急援助承诺时，

sentences.en: the Brazilian government, you know, wasn't ready to say, sure, we'll take the help.
sentences.zh: 巴西政府并没有准备好说：“好的，我们接受帮助。”

sentences.en: So all this outrage, all these online photos, all these alarmed messages, and this sense from Europe that this is a crisis that it can help solve.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有的这些愤怒、网上的照片、惊恐的信息，以及欧洲认为自己能帮助解决这场危机的感觉，

sentences.en: How is that looking and feeling to people inside Brazil?
sentences.zh: 在巴西国内的人看来和感受如何呢？

sentences.en: I think many Brazilians are deeply concerned about the fate of the Amazon, and they very much want their country to do more,
sentences.zh: 我认为许多巴西人对亚马逊的命运深感担忧，他们非常希望国家能做得更多，

sentences.en: to rein in deforestation and to pay attention to the messages that we're hearing from across the world.
sentences.zh: 以遏制森林砍伐，并重视我们从世界各地听到的声音。

sentences.en: You know, however, this is a very bitterly polarized society.
sentences.zh: 然而，这是一个社会矛盾极其尖锐的国家。

sentences.en: And on the flip side of that, I think many people resent the idea that European powers would bark down orders to a former colony and tell it how it needs to administer its affairs.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我认为许多人反感欧洲列强对前殖民地发号施令，教导它如何管理自身事务的做法。

sentences.en: And that's certainly the approach the president has taken.
sentences.zh: 这当然也是总统所采取的态度。

sentences.en: He recently said that if the Europeans had, you know, many million dollars to spend on conservation efforts, that they should plant some trees in their own countries.
sentences.zh: 他最近表示，如果欧洲人有几百万美元用于环保工作，他们应该在自己的国家多植树。

sentences.en: So in Bolsonaro's mind, this is a Brazilian issue, and the rest of the world should essentially mind its own business.
sentences.zh: 所以在博索纳罗看来，这是巴西的内部事务，世界其他国家基本上应该少管闲事。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: He says the Amazon is ours, and we're not going to entertain criticism or prescriptions from countries that many years ago raised down their own forests and, you know,
sentences.zh: 他说亚马逊是我们的，我们不会理会那些多年前就砍光了自己森林，并以此发展经济的国家所提出的批评或建议，

sentences.en: grew their economies in doing so.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们就是靠那样发展起来的。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's been his position, and it's hard to see him backing down.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是他的立场，而且很难看到他会做出让步。

sentences.en: It's interesting, Ernesto, as we're talking about this, I'm realizing that as horrifying as the development of the rainforest might feel to people watching from the outside,
sentences.zh: 埃内斯托，这很有趣，我们在谈论这件事时，我意识到，尽管外界观察者对雨林的开发感到恐惧，

sentences.en: and as scary as these fires are, it does seem unusual for other countries to tell a country what it can and can't do with its resources.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些火灾令人害怕，但其他国家告诉一个国家如何处理其资源，这似乎确实很不寻常。

sentences.en: You know, if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果美国

sentences.en: theoretically wants to blow up the Grand Canyon or log entire national parks, those might be insane ideas, but no one can stop the United States from doing that.
sentences.zh: 理论上想要炸掉大峡谷或砍伐整个国家公园，这些想法可能很疯狂，但没人能阻止美国这样做。

sentences.en: You know, if we want to frack in West Virginia, it's up to us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们想在西弗吉尼亚州进行水力压裂开采，那也是我们自己的事。

sentences.en: It's our land.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的土地。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Many Brazilians say, hey, this is our territory.
sentences.zh: 许多巴西人说：嘿，这是我们的领土。

sentences.en: This is our land.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的土地。

sentences.en: Don't mess with our sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 别干涉我们的主权。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, you know, the Amazon is a unique and special and irreplaceable place.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，亚马逊是一个独特、特殊且不可替代的地方。

sentences.en: And, you know, if we contemplate the possibility that some 50 years from now, it will disappear or become a fraction of itself, the consequences are very significant.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果我们考虑到50年后它可能消失或仅存一小部分的可能性，后果是非常严重的。

sentences.en: The Amazon is a repository of carbon.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊是一个碳库。

sentences.en: So if it vanishes, there will be lots of carbon that will be released back into the atmosphere, which will warm the planet.
sentences.zh: 如果它消失了，大量的碳将被释放回大气中，这将导致地球变暖。

sentences.en: And if as the rainforest diminishes, more of its land becomes cattle grazing pastures.
sentences.zh: 而且随着雨林减少，更多的土地会变成牛群放牧的牧场。

sentences.en: You know, that also would contribute to warming because cattle grazing is one of the top emitters of greenhouse gas.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这也将加剧变暖，因为畜牧业是温室气体的主要排放源之一。

sentences.en: And so the rest of the world does have a stake in this fight.
sentences.zh: 所以世界其他国家确实与这场斗争息息相关。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: You know, I think right now the Brazilian government is in no mood to open the door for this debate and to have sort of a global discussion about the fate of the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我认为目前巴西政府没有心情开启这场辩论，也没有心情就亚马逊的命运进行全球性讨论。

sentences.en: But it's facing the real possibility of a boycott of its products, which people have been warning about on social media, and of a core trade deal that may now be on thin ice.
sentences.zh: 但它正面临着产品被抵制的现实可能性——社交媒体上人们一直在警告这一点——而且一项核心贸易协定现在也岌岌可危。

sentences.en: And if we see this debate going on for months, Brazil might be forced to come to the negotiating table and have this moment of reckoning with others across the world.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看到这场辩论持续数月，巴西可能会被迫坐到谈判桌前，与世界各地的人们进行一次清算。

sentences.en: Ernesto, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 埃内斯托，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: My pleasure, Michael.
sentences.zh: 不客气，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, after initially rejecting $22 million in aid from the countries of the G7
sentences.zh: 周二，在最初拒绝了七国集团国家提供的2200万美元援助后，

sentences.en: to fight the fires in the Amazon, Brazil's government said it might accept the aid under certain conditions.
sentences.zh: 巴西政府表示，在特定条件下可能会接受这笔援助。

sentences.en: President Bolsonaro said he would take the money if France's president, Emmanuel Macron,
sentences.zh: 博索纳罗总统表示，如果法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙

sentences.en: apologized for remarks about Brazil and its environmental record that Bolsonaro said he found offensive.
sentences.zh: 为他关于巴西及其环境记录的言论道歉，博索纳罗认为这些言论具有冒犯性，他就会接受这笔钱。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: During an emotional hearing in Manhattan on Wednesday, more than a dozen victims of Jeffrey Epstein's alleged sexual abuse told their stories to a federal judge
sentences.zh: 周三在曼哈顿举行的一场情绪激动的听证会上，十几名杰弗里·爱泼斯坦涉嫌性虐待的受害者向联邦法官讲述了她们的故事，

sentences.en: and assailed a criminal justice system that they said had failed them.
sentences.zh: 并抨击了她们所说的辜负了她们的刑事司法系统。

sentences.en: It makes me sick to my stomach that there's perpetrators out there that obviously helped him in many ways for a very long time, and they're still out there with no punishment.
sentences.zh: 想到外面还有那些在很长一段时间里以各种方式帮助过他的施暴者，而且他们至今逍遥法外，没有受到任何惩罚，我就感到恶心。

sentences.en: The hearing was held to officially dismiss the charges against Epstein following his suicide, which leaves prosecutors with no defendant to try.
sentences.zh: 举行这次听证会是为了在爱泼斯坦自杀后正式撤销对他的指控，这导致检察官没有被告可以审判。

sentences.en: But it gave his accusers a rare chance to speak out.
sentences.zh: 但这给了他的指控者一个难得的发声机会。

sentences.en: Several of the women in the courtroom addressed their remarks to the prosecutors, urging them to keep investigating Epstein's employees and associates,
sentences.zh: 法庭上的几名女性向检察官发表了讲话，敦促他们继续调查爱泼斯坦的员工和同伙，

sentences.en: who they said acted as his accomplices.
sentences.zh: 她们称这些人充当了他的帮凶。

sentences.en: I was recruited at a very young age from Mar-a-Lago
sentences.zh: 我在很小的时候就从海湖庄园被招募，

sentences.en: and entrapped in a world that I didn't understand, and I've been fighting that very world to this day, and I won't stop fighting.
sentences.zh: 并被困在一个我不了解的世界里，直到今天我仍在与那个世界抗争，我不会停止抗争。

sentences.en: I will never be silenced until these people are brought to justice.
sentences.zh: 在这些人被绳之以法之前，我绝不会保持沉默。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
